Latin word

praestō

praestō, praestāre, praestitī, praestitum

verb, first conjugation, with the dative of those surpassed and the ablative of the respect · Conjugation on Wiktionary

stand out, have the advantage over, be better than; guarantee, answer for, vouch for; answer for, be responsible for; perform, fulfil (a duty)

In this lexicon

  • advantage

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.2.2: cum virtūte omnibus praestārent; Cic. Inv. 1.5: quā rē hominēs bēstiīs praestent (Lewis & Short)

  • guarantee

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.3: praestābō sūmptum nusquam melius posse pōnī; Cic. Fam. 1.4.3: Ego tibi ā vī … praestāre nihil possum

  • liability

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 6.1.4: ut nihil in vītā nōbīs praestandum praeter culpam putēmus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 6.3.5: quem tamen ego praestāre nōn poteram (Lewis & Short)

  • perform

    also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.7.8: praestāre dominō sī pār officium potes; Cic. de Or. 2.38 (Lewis & Short): suum mūnus; Traupman 359

  • praestō esse (+ dat.): at your service

    classical

  • praestō esse: available

    classical

  • praestō esse: available

    classical

Examples

  • praestābō sūmptum nusquam melius posse pōnī

    I guarantee the money could not be better spent anywhereCic. Q. fr. 3.1.3

    In the entry for guarantee

  • Ego tibi ā vī, hāc praesertim imbēcillitāte magistrātuum, praestāre nihil possum

    Against violence, especially with the magistrates as weak as they are, I can guarantee you nothingCic. Fam. 1.4.3

    In the entry for guarantee

  • quis potest praestāre semper sapientem beātum fore, cum vel in omnibus hīs ūnō tempore esse possit?

    who can guarantee that the wise man will always be happy, when he may meet all these at one and the same time?Cic. Tusc. 5.29

    In the entry for guarantee

  • simus eā mente ut nihil in vītā nōbīs praestandum praeter culpam putēmus

    let us be of a mind to think that in life we must answer for nothing but our own wrongdoingCic. Fam. 6.1.4 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for liability
